problem: The troposphere is described as extending 'from the surface to about 8–12 km'. That is a mid-latitude figure; over India the tropopause sits near 16–17 km, so a student may think the model stops well below the real path.
fix: The troposphere is the neutral lower atmosphere, about 11 km thick in mid-latitudes and up to roughly 16–17 km over the tropics; almost all of the delay comes from the lowest few kilometres.

problem: 'Four corrections are applied before the fix: satellite clock, orbit, ionosphere and troposphere' reads as if orbit error were a range correction added to the pseudorange. Orbit (ephemeris) data are used to compute the satellite position; only clock, ionosphere and troposphere are subtracted from the measured range.
fix: The broadcast ephemeris gives the satellite position and clock offset; these are used first. Then ionospheric and tropospheric delays are subtracted from each pseudorange before the fix.

problem: Symbols are typed with underscores and carets (a_f0, a_f1, d_I, d_T, d_z, δt_s, 10^16), which a phone reader will misread.
fix: Use the subscript and superscript tags: a<sub>f0</sub>, a<sub>f1</sub>, a<sub>f2</sub>, d<sub>I</sub>, d<sub>T</sub>, d<sub>z</sub>, δt<sub>s</sub>, 10<sup>16</sup> electrons/m².
